newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees better expense control in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees better expense control in Q4.

text.p: Xerox Corp said on Friday that third quarter document processing expenses grew faster than revenues, slowing earnings growth, but the company expects "some improvement" during the fourth quarter.
In a statement, Xerox Chairman Paul Allaire said, "We expect some improvement in the fourth quarter, with somewhat slower growth in costs and expenses."

The company today reported third quarter fully diluted earnings from continuing operations of $0.68 per share, up from $0.65 a year earlier. The consensus Wall Street forecast had called for Xerox to earn $0.82 per share.
The surprise earnings disappointment sent the stock reeling in pre-open trading and led to a delay at the opening of the New York Stock Exchange for an imbalance.
At 1018 EDT/1418 GMT the stock was off 10 at 46 in heavy trading.
The company said revenues from its document processing business fell two percent in the third quarter, to $250 million from $256 million a year ago.
Black-and-white copier revenues, which accounted for 56 percent of total corporate revenues, declined four percent in the quarter, it said.
Total revenues grew four percent in the quarter, to $4.2 billion from $4.0 billion last year.
The company said black-and-white copier revenues declined as a result of several factors, including price pressure and difficult economic environments in Europe and a number of emerging markets.
Allaire said, "We continue to be optimistic about 1997...We've made investments in our sales force and new products which will increase our competitiveness in the market."

He said gross margins improved by an unspecified amount during the quarter, but expenses outpaced revenues as Xerox continued to invest in document outsourcing sales operations and to accelerate product development.

"During the balance of the year, our objectives are to capitalize on these investments, continue to improve gross margins, and ensure that selling, administrative and general expense growth does not exceed revenue growth," he said.
"I am disappointed in the results this quarter," Allaire said.
"Although enterprise printing revenue growth accelerated in all major geographic areas, overall revenue growth was adversely affected by a modest decline in black-and-white copier revenues," he said.
He added, "Our investments in sales coverage and promotion did not yield the results we expected in the quarter."

Total revenues on a pre-currency basis grew 5.0 percent, with end-user equipment sales growing 6.0 percent. Digital enterprise printing revenues grew 23 percent. Enterprise printing now represents 30 percent of total revenues.
Geographically, it said a significant slowdown in growth in Brazil followed two years of exceptional growth.

Document processing revenues in the United States grew five percent in the quarter, while Rank Xerox revenues increased two percent and revenues in other operations grew six percent. Xerox did not specify revenue figures in these various categories.

As a result of hiring in the company's fast-growing document outsourcing business, it said worldwide employment increased during the quarter by 400, to 87,000. Hiring in sales and manufacturing was offset by reductions in other areas.
Gross profit grew four percent.

Research and development expenses rose eight percent, and selling, administrative and general expenses grew 10 percent, somewhat faster than anticipated, primarily as a result of additional investments in sales coverage and promotion, new product advertising and marketing support.
The company's insurance and other financial services businesses are reported as discontinued operations.
-- Eric Auchard, New York Newsdesk 212-859-1736
